human_summary: A fatal road crash occurred early on 20 December 2024 at a police checkpoint near Neela Market intersection on Purbachal 300 Feet Road in Rupganj, Narayanganj. A passenger car struck a stationary motorcycle carrying three BUET students, killing 22-year-old Muhtasim (Mohtassim) Masud, a second-year CSE student, and seriously injuring his two friends, Amit Saha and Mehedi Hasan [ev_7a9911d957c3b042][ev_f6979130e8086261][ev_3cb89b4791adcc04]. Sources consistently report the motorcycle had been stopped by police when the car hit it; the car was described as speeding in reports [ev_17797e3df968c79a][ev_850f0b4bcf2418e4]. The video analysis shows severe front-end damage to a passenger car but does not establish crash dynamics [ev_07a4549765a2d7a1]. A claim that the accused were intoxicated appears only in an on-screen headline and is not independently confirmed [ev_07a4549765a2d7a1]. The victim's father filed a case under the Road Transport Act 2018 at Rupganj Police Station, and three accused were arrested and later sent to jail by a Narayanganj court [ev_6f614cdd3f691d5e][ev_23e903df4479a2d7][ev_e8c697e231ce67eb]. The body was sent to Shaheed Suhrawardy Medical College Hospital for postmortem [ev_1f834f7777ccf794]. Location precision is limited to the named intersection; exact coordinates are not available. Independent sources include The Daily Star, Prothom Alo, TBS, Dhaka Tribune, and ATN News video analysis, with six independent sources counted after accounting for a possible duplicate group [ev_7e2b75efeb5007b6][ev_4868bd0517e733cd][ev_4c5ab42977ec172a][ev_23e903df4479a2d7][ev_07a4549765a2d7a1].

Reports indicate a Sylhet-bound Bengal Paribahan bus and a Dhaka-bound Unique Paribahan bus were involved. The collision was described as head-on, with a video circulating showing the Bengal bus losing control and hitting the Unique bus, which then fell into a roadside ditch [ev_8675a512af387063][ev_99685340cfb96e6d][ev_e7e4274f75924b4d]. Casualty figures conflict: Prothom Alo reports eight killed and at least 25 injured, while The Daily Star reports nine passengers of the Unique bus died and at least 24 injured [ev_a50c19158fca4347][ev_f4f6bf3ae3a5ae94]. The exact time also varies: around 7:00 am vs. 7:30 am [ev_8675a512af387063][ev_a50c19158fca4347]. Location precision is area-level, coordinates represent the Kashikapan area centroid. Witnesses claim the Bengal bus attempted to overtake a pickup, veering into oncoming traffic, though this remains an allegation [ev_e7e4274f75924b4d]. The incident was covered by two independent sources. No traffic effects or emergency response details were provided. Key uncertainties include exact casualty counts, precise time of the crash, and confirmation of the overtaking narrative.

human_summary: Evidence from The Daily Star and a video report from Ekattor TV describe a fatal bus crash on the Bogura-Naogaon regional highway near Erulia Bazar in Bogura Sadar upazila. The Daily Star reports that a speeding bus ran over labourers waiting for work around 5:30 am, killing seven; the video report confirms seven fatalities. The bus, operated by Shah Fateh Ali Paribahan, had reportedly been running without a route permit for one and a half years per BRTA. A fire service officer stated that brake failure occurred when the bus gave way to a motorcycle, after which it struck an electricity pole and then hit the labourers. Authorities formed a three-member committee led by Additional District Magistrate Masud Hossain to investigate; compensation of Tk 25,000 per deceased and Tk 15,000 per injured was announced. Locals blocked the road demanding speed breakers, and the Roads and Highways Department promised installation. The crash killed seven and injured an unspecified number; the broader article mentions 16 deaths and 48 injuries across Sylhet and Bogura, but this incident-specific count is seven. The exact crash coordinates remain unknown; geolocation is based on city-level centroid. [ev_3d9b6f7ef1b8f36b, ev_7d10439deaca950c, ev_b02f78dc220fb6ca, ev_35ec9cf7714b6c1c]
